column1: # Counties and regions written on their own line between the post town and the postcode. Columns: country (GB = the United Kingdom, IE = Ireland), name (any case, accents and hyphens as usual).

# A line is read as a county only when a post town stands before it; a name that is also a town of its own (Durham, Antrim, Armagh, Down) counts as a county only with "County" or "Co." in front (or, for the Irish

# counties, on its own line after a place). Royal Mail's PAF Programmers' Guide calls the county optional and prints it after the post town; the UPU Ireland sheet prints "CO. CORK" on a line of its own.
# The names are our own list of the ceremonial, preserved and historic counties of Britain and the counties of Ireland (geographic facts, no external file).
